title: Did Baby Hanuman Swallow the Sun?
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 4(65) and Uttara Kanda 7(35-36) (Critical Edition; vulgate 4.66, 7.35-36)

captions.instagram:
Did baby Hanuman really swallow the sun?

Many of us grew up singing that baby Hanuman swallowed the sun, thinking it was a sweet fruit. Valmiki tells this story twice. In the Kishkindha Kanda, Jambavan tells Hanuman that as a child he leapt at the rising sun, flew three hundred yojanas, and was pushed back by its heat, without losing heart. In the Uttara Kanda, the Wind god keeps him cool, he reaches the sun's chariot, then chases Rahu and even Indra's elephant Airavata. In both, Indra's thunderbolt breaks his left jaw, and that is how he got his name: Hanuman. Neither telling has him swallow the sun. That comes from a beautiful line of the Hanuman Chalisa (chaupai 18): “Jug sahasra jojan par bhanu, leelyo tahi madhur phal janu”, the sun, yug-sahasra yojanas away, swallowed as a sweet fruit. We sing it with devotion; Valmiki tells it differently.

Did you know how Hanuman got his name? Next: why Hanuman forgot his own powers 👇

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 4(65) and Uttara Kanda 7(35-36) (Critical Edition; vulgate 4.66, 7.35-36)

Verses:
• Valmiki tells the episode twice: Jambavan to Hanuman (Kishkindha) and Agastya to Rama (Uttara) — 4.65.1-2, 7.35.1
• As a child he saw the rising sun, thought it a fruit, and leapt into the sky — 4.65.19, 7.35.23-24
• After 300 yojanas, driven back by the sun's radiance, he was not dejected — 4.65.20
• In the Uttara telling, Vayu keeps him cool, the sun does not burn him, and he comes near the sun — 7.35.28-30
• He meets Rahu on the sun's chariot, chases him, then runs at Airavata thinking it a great fruit — 7.35.31-44
• Indra's thunderbolt strikes him; he falls on a mountain and his left jaw breaks — 4.65.21-22, 7.35.46-47
• He is named Hanuman because his jaw (hanu) was injured — 4.65.22, 7.36.11
• Neither telling has him swallow the sun — 4.65.19-22, 7.35.23-47 (read)
• The swallowing comes from the Hanuman Chalisa: 'जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू। लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू॥' — Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 18

claims.claim: Valmiki tells the episode twice: Jambavan to Hanuman (Kishkindha) and Agastya to Rama (Uttara)
As a child he saw the rising sun, thought it a fruit, and leapt into the sky
After 300 yojanas, driven back by the sun's radiance, he was not dejected
In the Uttara telling, Vayu keeps him cool, the sun does not burn him, and he comes near the sun
He meets Rahu on the sun's chariot, chases him, then runs at Airavata thinking it a great fruit
Indra's thunderbolt strikes him; he falls on a mountain and his left jaw breaks
He is named Hanuman because his jaw (hanu) was injured
Neither telling has him swallow the sun
The swallowing comes from the Hanuman Chalisa: 'जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू। लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू॥'

verify_note: CE 4.65.19: as a child he saw the rising sun, wanted to seize it as a fruit, and leapt into the sky. 4.65.20: after 300 yojanas, driven back by its radiance, not dejected. 4.65.21-22: Indra hurls the thunderbolt; on a mountain peak his left jaw breaks; hence the name Hanuman. (Narrated by Jambavan to Hanuman, 4.65.1-2.) CE 7.35.23-24: sees the rising sun like hibiscus, flies up wanting the fruit. 7.35.28-30: Vayu keeps him cool; he comes near the sun; the sun does not burn him. 7.35.31-44: meets Rahu on the sun's chariot; chases Rahu, then Airavata ('this too is a great fruit'). 7.35.46-47: Indra's thunderbolt; falls on the mountain; left jaw broken. 7.36.11: Indra: named Hanuman because his jaw (hanu) was injured. No swallowing of the sun in either telling. Hanuman Chalisa: 'जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू। लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू॥'
